clusters.name: Jonah leaving home, 1991–1992
clusters.reason: Around Jonah beginning at the conservatory in September 1991, within months: he leaned hard on his friend Rafe and fused with him; a wrist injury stopped his playing in October and his anxiety rose and functioning fell; he and Rafe clashed and Rafe moved out in November; he was on his own, getting high, absorbed in fixing radios; in January 1992, lost and low, unable to get going, with his grandfather gone and his mother about to remarry, too much was moving at once. His grandfather Gordon died in June 1991, months before. The shifts pile close together from autumn through winter and into spring; his functioning recovered slowly through the spring holiday when he earned money fixing radios.

clusters.name: Tara's birth, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: Around the fall of 1989 when Jonah settled with his mother and Desmond in the rebuilt Hollin Road house, beside when he liked late nights: he shifted to late nights and unsure whether that was out of the ordinary; his mother's father Clifford came back into the family early that year. In July 1990 Tara was born to his father and Bettina. By January 1994, he was stung that his dad had never heard of the film he was making, and anxiety rose. His cousin Bella was treated for melanoma around the same time. The exchange to Lisbon and Porto came that year and he tore through the rest of his degree; things improved. The shifts are Jonah's own across these years, apart from Tara's birth and his cousin's illness, and show a climb through secondary school alongside new household arrangements.

clusters.name: Jonah's burnout and move, 2001–2008
clusters.reason: Around September 2001 when Jonah was running out of steam for performing and his anxiety rose and functioning fell, beside his grandmother Winifred being found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002: in February 2002 he had a disastrous audition for the national orchestra and his functioning fell further; by September 2002 he was on poor terms with family and friends and distanced himself. He left Thornbury for Gull Harbour in September 2002, met Marisol at a winter party in January 2003, moved to Fenwick in June 2003 to live with her, and split up within the year in October 2003. Once they split, he sank into a deep depression that took hold that winter. He returned to Thornbury in November 2003, could not face his family, and relied gingerly on friends. His grandmother's final months were spent in Maureen and Desmond's home in September 2003 and she died in February 2004. By August 2008, when he moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school, he stopped speaking to his mother, a cutoff that held for roughly a year. The shifts in his functioning, his distance from family, and his anxiety pile across years around his burnout and his grandmother's decline, with the depression deepening after his split with Marisol.

clusters.name: Lorna's death and Jonah's nursing school, 2008
clusters.reason: Around January 2008 when Jonah's grandmother Lorna died: in July 2008, four weeks before nursing school, Jonah was at Alder Creek building with Silas and too drained for conversation with his mother; she pressed to visit him, his anxiety rose, and he kept the door shut on her when she came. His aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009, with months of rehabilitation. By August 2008 when he left for nursing school at Marlow Sound, he stopped speaking to his mother. The shifts are in Jonah's relationship moves away from his mother and in her pressing toward him, with his anxiety rising around the visit; Lorna's death opens the period, though Jonah's own distancing and the move to nursing school carry it forward.

clusters.name: Jonah married to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around March 2017 when Jonah married Wren: he saw his mother a bit less once Wren came along. In October 2017, his cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in her forties. By October 2019, Wren was swamped, one thing after another, her symptom and anxiety rose and functioning fell; Jonah was too strict laying out a plan to settle her, his anxiety rose and he overfunctioned; Wren talked with her father and brother all day, fusion with them; then she settled once the weekend had a plan and her anxiety fell and functioning rose. At the lake house for Frances's retirement on October 22–23, Jonah was awake from the small hours with no more sleep and could only pull back as the others rose, his symptom and anxiety rose and he distanced; Wren was anxious when he had had no sleep at family occasions, and long quiet drives home followed. The shifts pile around the changes in Jonah's household and his place in Wren's family, with heightened anxiety and symptom on both sides around family gatherings.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
